newsitem.title: USA: Michaels Stores debt rises before results.
newsitem.headline: Michaels Stores debt rises before results.

text.p: Michael Stores Inc debt traded up over a point on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday's release of the retailer's fourth quarter earnings, high-yield traders said.
The company's 10-7/8 percent notes due 2006 were quoted 1-1/2 points higher at 103 bid, traders said.
"Currently, we haven't released anything," said Brandon Shelley, corporate communications specialist at Michaels Stores Inc.
"The company's quarterly earnings will be released via conference call on Wednesday after the close of the market," Shelly added.
Last week, the retailer reported an eight percent increae in February sales to $97.9 million from $90.4 million in the prior year. The company also said February same-store sales rose 5.0 percent.
Currently, Michaels Stores' senior unsecured debt is rated Ba2 by Moody's Investors Service Inc and BB-minus by Standard & Poor's. Its subordinated debt is rated B1 by Moody's and single-B by S&P.
Michaels Stores, based in Irving, Texas, is the largest specialty retailer of arts and crafts with over 448 stores in the U.S.
On Tuesday, the company's stock was quoted off 1/4 at 17-3/8.
